info.title: Shop Admin API
info.description: Endpoints used by the admin panel.

get.description: Catalogue numbers and the queues of work for every staff member: each queue only for the roles that handle it (`queues` fields are null for the others), counted up to 1000. The number of products is an estimate of the database (null before its first statistics). The sales of today, the last 7 and the last 30 days of completed hours only for administrators (`sales` is null for other roles). The system status (services, outbox, queues, search index) only for administrators; for other roles `system` is null. A service that is down, a broker whose management API does not answer (`queues` is null) or a search index that cannot be counted (`indexedProducts` is null, `inSync` is false) does not fail the request.

get.description: A page of products, drafts included, sorted by name (by default) or by `sort`, then by id. Every staff member may read it. Page with the opaque `next` cursor as `after`, with the same filters and sort (a cursor of another sort is a 400); the first page (without `after`) also has the `total` of the matching products, counted up to 10 000. The category filter includes the subcategories and the products that have the category as an additional one; an unknown category gives 404. The search term is a literal part of the name, case-insensitive.

put.description: Replaces the whole data of the product (a form save). Administrators and marketing only. Send the `version` of the view the edit is based on: another current version is a 409 and nothing is overwritten. A successful save raises the version even when the data did not change. A row of `variants` with the `variantId` of the product keeps that variant, a row with `null` is a new one; a variant missing from the rows is removed. An empty `slug` derives it from the name, or keeps the slug once the product was published. The product records the staff member of the token and the time of the change.

post.summary: Upload the original of a product image
post.description: Stores one image file in the image storage and answers with its key and a preview. Administrators and marketing only. One file per request, in the `file` field of a `multipart/form-data` body; send several files one after another. JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF and HEIC are accepted, decided by the content and not by the name, up to 64 MB and 50 megapixels. The key follows the content, so the same file always gives the same key and is stored once. Name the key in `images[].key` of a product write; an original that no product names stays in the storage. The `detail` of a 422 is a Polish text for the staff member.

Page with the opaque `next` cursor as `after`, with the same filters and sort (a cursor of another sort is a 400); the first page (without `after`) also has the `total` of the matching products, counted up to 10 000. The category filter includes the subcategories and the products that have the category as an additional one; an unknown category gives 404. The search term is a literal part of the name, case-insensitive. With `level` the page is of the products at that stock level and the first page has the `total` of them.

Counting what the stock has changes nothing: the version stays and no history entry is recorded. The history entry names the staff member of the token.

get.description: A page of orders, newest first (then by id) or in the order of `sort` (by the moment of placement or by the amount, then by id); with `refund=pending` only the orders with a refund to do, the nearest due date first (then by id), with `refund=overdue` only those past their due date (a subset of the pending ones in the same order, so the cursor of one leads the other); both take no `sort` and no range of days. The status filter, the search and the range of days combine with it (the search with `refund=pending` too); sorting by the amount takes no search and no range of days. The search `q` is an exact order number (`R-100001`, any letter case), or a complete email address (a domain with a dot), exactly and in any letter case, otherwise a fragment of 3 to 100 characters of the number, the email or the name (any letter case, `%` and `_` mean themselves; `jan@gm` is a fragment); anything else is a 400 at `q`. `placedFrom` and `placedTo` are days of Europe/Warsaw (`YYYY-MM-DD`, both included), `placedFrom` after `placedTo` is a 400. Page with the opaque `nextCursor` as `after`, with the same filters and sort (a cursor of another sort is a 400); the first page (without `after`) also has the `total` of the matching orders, counted up to 10 000. With `customerId` only the orders of that customer, newest first, with the status filter only (its history on the card of the customer). Administrators, support and the warehouse only.

parameters.name: refund

estimated.description: Always true: the number is an estimate.

productCount.description: The estimated number of products. Null while the database has no statistics of the products yet (they are refreshed after a mass change and by the autovacuum).

DashboardQueuesResponse.description: The work waiting for the staff member. Every queue is counted up to 1000 (`capped`: more than that) by the module that owns it, and is null when the staff member has no access to the queue: the roles are listed with each field.

paidToShip.description: Paid orders waiting for shipping (`/orders?status=paid`). Administrators, support, warehouse.

awaitingPayment.description: Orders not paid yet (`/orders?status=new`). Administrators and support.

pendingRefunds.description: Refunds to do (`/orders?refund=pending`). Administrators and support.

overdueRefunds.description: Refunds past their due date (`/orders?refund=overdue`). Administrators and support.

outOfStockVariants.description: Variants with nothing available (`/inventory?level=out_of_stock`). Administrators and warehouse.

lowStockVariants.description: Variants with 1 to 5 available (`/inventory?level=low_stock`). Administrators and warehouse.

productsWithoutImages.description: Products with no image (`/products?images=none`). Administrators and marketing.

DashboardSalesPeriodResponse.description: The sales of one period. Amounts in grosze. Every field is null for a period without a completed hour (today between 0:00 and 1:00).

orderCount.description: The number of orders paid in the period.

averageOrderValue.description: Revenue per order in grosze, rounded half up; null without orders.

changeBasisPoints.description: The change of the revenue against the period before in basis points (1250 is +12.5%), rounded half away from zero; null when the period before had no revenue.

DashboardSalesResponse.description: The sales of completed hours, summed from an hourly pre-aggregation by Ordering: revenue is the gross total (after discounts) of the orders paid in the period by the moment of their payment; a later cancellation or refund does not lower it. `today` runs from midnight of the Polish clock to `dataUntil` and is compared with yesterday from midnight to the same hour of the clock (on the days the clock changes the two may differ by an hour of real time); between 0:00 and 1:00 every field of `today` is null. `last7Days` and `last30Days` are the last 168 and 720 hours, compared with as many hours before them.

dataUntil.description: The end of every period: the start of the current hour (UTC). The current hour is not counted.

DashboardServiceResponse.description: The state of one service of the stack.

latencyMs.description: How long the service took to answer, in milliseconds. Null when it is down.

pending.description: Events waiting to be relayed to the broker.

DashboardQueueResponse.description: A queue of the message broker.

consumers.description: Number of AMQP subscribers (basic.consume) of the queue, as reported by RabbitMQ. The Messenger worker polls with basic.get instead of subscribing, so this is 0 even while the worker runs: it says nothing about the worker.

ready.description: Messages that a worker could take now (not handed to a worker, due), counted up to 1000.

oldestReadyAgeSeconds.description: How long the oldest ready message has been ready, in seconds (a delayed message from the moment it became due). Null without a ready message.

stalled.description: Whether the oldest ready message waits longer than the limit of the API (600 s): nothing takes the messages of the queue.

DashboardMessagesResponse.description: The messages of the queues in the database (the outbox and the commands), judged by the API.

healthy.description: Nothing is in `failed` and no queue stands.

transports.description: Always in this order: outbox, scheduled, payment_simulator, promotions, jobs.

services.description: Always in this order: postgres, redis, elasticsearch, rabbitmq, keycloak, garage, imgproxy, mailpit. A service that does not answer within 1 s is down.

queues.description: Queues of the broker. Null when its management API does not answer.

sales.description: Null unless the staff member is an administrator.

system.description: Null unless the staff member is an administrator.
